subject: Pharmacology
vignette: A 24-year-old man with epilepsy has been taking phenytoin 300 mg/day with a serum concentration of 12 micrograms/mL. After the dose is increased to 400 mg/day, the concentration rises to 28 micrograms/mL and he develops nystagmus and ataxia.
question: Which of the following best explains this finding?
explanation_correct: Phenytoin, like ethanol and high-dose aspirin, follows zero-order (saturable) elimination: once hepatic enzymes are saturated, a constant amount of drug is eliminated per unit time, so a small dose increase can produce a disproportionately large rise in serum concentration and toxicity.

explanation_incorrect.B: A change in volume of distribution would not produce this disproportionate rise at steady state.
explanation_incorrect.C: Decreased protein binding would lower total drug concentration rather than raising it sharply.
explanation_incorrect.D: Phenytoin is metabolized hepatically, not cleared unchanged by the kidney.
explanation_incorrect.E: Enzyme induction would lower serum concentrations rather than raise them.

educationalObjective: Phenytoin shows zero-order (saturable) elimination, so small dose increases can cause large, toxic rises in serum concentration.
